unit.title: Organize, prepare and present simple dishes

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does "mise en place" mean in a kitchen?
options: Cleaning down the kitchen after the last dish has gone out
Having everything weighed, cut and ready before you cook
Putting the cooked food on the plate in a neat, tidy way
Writing the day's menu and pinning it up on the wall

questions.stem: A recipe for 4 portions needs 500 g of rice. How much rice do you need for 8 portions?
options: 1 kg

questions.stem: Lunch at the villa is at 1:00 p.m. The stew needs 90 minutes to cook. What is the latest time it can go on the stove?
options: 12:00 noon

questions.stem: Why do you write a time plan before you cook a meal with several dishes?
options: So that every dish is ready and hot at the right time
So that each dish can be cooked as slowly as possible
So that the guests can see what time you started work
So that you will not need to read the recipes at all

questions.stem: You check the food delivered to the villa kitchen. Which item should you send back?
options: Carrots that are firm and bright orange
Eggs that are clean, with no cracks in the shells
Chicken that feels warm and has a sour smell
Fish with clear eyes and firm, shiny flesh

questions.stem: Which fresh ackee is safe to prepare and cook?
options: Ackee from pods that opened by themselves on the tree
Ackee from pods that were forced open while still shut
Ackee picked green and left to ripen in a closed bag
Ackee cooked with the seeds and pink membrane left in

questions.stem: Why do you soak or boil saltfish before you use it in ackee and saltfish?
options: To make the fish turn a bright white colour
To add more flavour to the fish before cooking
To make the small bones go soft enough to eat
To remove most of the salt

questions.stem: Unless the Centre's food safety plan says otherwise, at what temperature should cold food such as salad and milk be kept?
options: 5 °C or below
10 °C or below
15 °C or below
20 °C or below

questions.stem: Which is the right way to dress for work in the kitchen?
options: Own clothes, hair loose, and a watch to keep track of time
Clean uniform, with rings and a bracelet for a smart look
Clean uniform and apron, hair tied back and covered, no rings
Yesterday's uniform, if it does not look dirty, and slippers

questions.stem: Chicken is safely cooked when the thickest part reaches about which core temperature (or as the Centre's food safety plan says)?
Hot food waiting to be served should be kept at about which temperature or above (or as the Centre's food safety plan says)?
Which is the safest way to thaw a frozen chicken?
options: On the counter overnight, so it is ready by the morning
Out in the sun on the back step, covered with a cloth
In the fridge, in a covered tray on the bottom shelf
In a bowl of hot water from the kettle for one hour

questions.stem: Where in the fridge should raw meat be stored?
options: On the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food
On the top shelf, above the cooked food
In the door shelves, next to the milk and the juice
Anywhere, as long as the fridge is cold

questions.stem: Why do many kitchens use colour-coded chopping boards?
options: To make the kitchen look bright and cheerful
To show which cook owns which of the boards
To tell the guests which food is raw or cooked
To keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food

questions.stem: Which is a time when a cook must wash their hands?
options: Only at the start of the shift each morning
After touching raw chicken, before touching salad
Only when the hands look dirty or greasy
Only after the cleaning at the end of the day

questions.stem: Where does a food handler in Jamaica get a Food Handler's Permit?
options: The local health department
The Jamaica Tourist Board
The Bureau of Standards
The parish tax office

questions.stem: A guest at the villa tells you she is allergic to peanuts. What should the cook do?
options: Pick the peanuts off the top of the dish before serving it
Tell her there is only a little peanut, so it will be fine
Check every ingredient and keep her food away from peanuts
Cook her food in the same pan after giving it a quick wipe

questions.stem: Which of these foods is a common allergen (a food that can cause a harmful reaction in some people)?
options: Plain boiled white rice
Boiled yellow yam
Roast sweet potato
Shrimp and lobster

questions.stem: You put leftover cooked rice in the fridge. What must go on its label?
options: The name of the guest who ordered the rice
What the food is and the date it was made
The price of the rice and the shop it came from
The cook's phone number and the time of day

questions.stem: What does "first in, first out" mean in the store room?
options: Use the older stock before the newer stock
Use the newest stock first, as it is freshest
Put each delivery away wherever there is space
Order new stock only once the old stock is gone

questions.stem: You have a large pot of soup left over after lunch. How should you cool it?
options: Leave it in the pot on the stove until the next day
Put the full, hot pot straight into the fridge
Divide it into shallow trays and chill it quickly
Cover it and leave it on the counter for six hours

questions.stem: How should you carry a knife in a busy kitchen?
options: Point up, so the blade cannot touch your leg
In your apron pocket, so your hands are free
Held out in front, so people can see it coming
Point down, close to your side, and warn others

questions.stem: A knife slips off the work top and starts to fall. What should you do?
options: Try to catch it before it hits the floor
Step back and let it fall to the floor
Put your foot out to stop it from falling
Grab it by the handle as it goes past you

questions.stem: Why is a sharp knife safer to use than a blunt one?
options: It needs less force, so it is less likely to slip
It never cuts the skin, even if it does slip
It does not need to be washed as often after use
It can be left loose in the sink without danger

questions.stem: Which knife is best for small jobs such as peeling and trimming vegetables?
options: A bread knife
A carving knife
A paring knife
A meat cleaver

questions.stem: The safety guard on the food mixer is broken. What should you do?
options: Use it with care, keeping your hands well away
Take the guard off, since the mixer works without it
Hold the guard shut with tape until it is mended
Do not use it; report it and use another mixer

questions.stem: What does "simmer" mean?
options: Cook in liquid at a fast, rolling boil with big bubbles
Cook in liquid just below boiling, with small bubbles
Cook in hot oil until the outside is crisp and brown
Cook in a dry oven with hot air all round the food

questions.stem: Which method cooks food in the steam above boiling water, with the food not in the water?
options: Steaming
Poaching
Boiling
Stewing

questions.stem: Which method suits a tough cut of meat, such as oxtail?
options: Quick frying in a hot pan for two minutes
Fast grilling over a high flame for one minute
Slow stewing in liquid for a long time
Thin slicing and serving it without cooking

questions.stem: Why do you pat fish or chicken dry before putting it into hot oil?
options: Dry food soaks up more oil, so it tastes richer
Wet food cooks too fast and burns before it is done
Wet food will not change colour in hot oil at all
Water makes hot oil spit, and the oil can burn you

questions.stem: A pan of oil catches fire on the stove. What should you do?
options: Throw a jug of water on it to put the flames out fast
Turn off the heat and slide a lid or fire blanket over it
Carry the pan outside quickly so it can burn out there
Fan the flames with a damp towel until they die down

questions.stem: How is festival usually cooked?
options: Deep-fried in hot oil
Boiled in salted water
Steamed over a pot
Baked in a hot oven

questions.stem: What usually gives Jamaican rice and peas its colour and flavour?
options: Tomato paste and curry powder
Soy sauce and brown sugar
Red kidney beans and coconut milk
Food colouring and chicken stock cubes

questions.stem: Which is the best way to prepare a fresh garden salad for lunch?
options: Dress it in the morning so the flavour can soak in
Wash and dry the leaves, and dress just before serving
Leave it out in the sun so the leaves stay crisp
Use the leaves as they come, as washing makes them limp

questions.stem: What does a roux (flour cooked in butter or oil) do in a sauce?
options: It makes the sauce sweet
It keeps the sauce cold
It gives the sauce a red colour
It thickens the sauce

questions.stem: How should callaloo be cooked to keep its colour and goodness?
options: Steamed for a short time, until just tender
Boiled for an hour, until it turns brown
Left to soak overnight in salted water
Deep-fried in hot oil until it is crisp

questions.stem: How should a cook taste food while it is cooking?
options: With a finger, as it is quicker than a spoon
With the stirring spoon, then back into the pot
With a clean spoon each time you taste
Never, since cooks must not taste the food

questions.stem: Which plate is right for serving a hot main course?
options: A cold plate straight from the fridge
A plate with a small chip on the rim
A plate that is still wet from washing
A clean plate that has been warmed

questions.stem: What is a garnish?
options: A large extra portion of meat added to the plate
A small, edible item that adds colour and flavour
A sauce poured over the whole plate to hide gaps
A paper decoration that the guest must not eat

questions.stem: Why do cooks use the same size of spoon or ladle for each portion?
options: So every guest gets the same amount, and costs stay right
So the kitchen has fewer spoons and ladles to wash
So the food cools down faster before it is served
So guests can see which spoon was used for them

questions.stem: You see a drip of sauce on the rim of a plate that is ready to go out. What should you do?
options: Send it as it is, since the guest will not notice
Cover the drip with an extra piece of garnish
Wipe the rim with clean kitchen paper
Wipe it with the cloth used for the counter top

questions.stem: What is the right order for cleaning a chopping board after use?
options: Rinse in cold water, then dry with a used cloth
Scrape, wash, rinse, sanitise, then air-dry
Sanitise first, then wash, then wipe on an apron
Wipe with a damp cloth and put it straight back

questions.stem: Why must you never mix bleach with other cleaning products?
options: The bleach will stop smelling fresh
The mix will stain the counter top
The mix costs more money to make up
The mix can give off a poisonous gas

questions.stem: How should you deal with food waste in the kitchen?
options: Put it in a lidded bin, and empty the bin often
Leave it in an open box by the back door
Keep it under the sink until the end of the week
Wash it down the drain with plenty of hot water

questions.stem: In the morning you find the fridge thermometer reads 12 °C. What should you do?
options: Turn the dial and say nothing to anyone
Wait to see if it gets colder later in the day
Report it at once and check if the food is safe
Move all the food onto the counter until it is fixed

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name for the temperature range between about 5 °C and 63 °C, where bacteria grow fastest?
What tool do you push into the thickest part of cooked meat to check its core temperature?
Which permit must every food handler in Jamaica hold?
What is the name of the Jamaican flat bread made from grated cassava?
What cooking method gently cooks eggs or fish in hot liquid that is not boiling? Give one word.
A recipe for 6 portions uses 3 cups of flour. How many cups are needed for 2 portions?
In the common colour-coded system, what colour of chopping board is used for raw meat?
Which knife has a long blade with a saw-like (serrated) edge and is used to slice loaves?
What is the word for something in food, such as peanuts or shellfish, that can cause a harmful reaction in some people?
What do you call cooking food with dry heat in an oven, as for bread or rum cake? Give one word.
What is the word for the amount of one dish served to one person?
What is the Jamaican style of seasoning meat with a spicy paste of scotch bonnet pepper, escallion and thyme, then cooking it slowly over wood or coals?
What is the Jamaican name for allspice, the dried berry used in jerk and escoveitch fish?
After washing, what do you use on food-contact surfaces to kill most of the germs left on them?
What is the written list of ingredients, amounts and method for a dish called?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and organise your work to cook a two-course lunch for six guests at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would read the menu and each recipe, and work out the amounts needed for six portions. I would check the store room and the fridge, make a list of anything missing, and order or buy it in good time, checking the quality and dates when it arrives. Next I would write a simple time plan, working back from the serving time, so that long jobs such as stewing start first and quick jobs such as dressing the salad are done last. Before cooking I would wash my hands, put on a clean uniform and set up my mise en place: weigh, wash, peel and cut the ingredients, and get out the pots, knives, boards and serving plates. Then I would cook each dish to the recipe, taste it with a clean spoon, warm the plates, serve on time and clean as I go.
markingPoints: Reads the menu and recipes and works out the amounts for six portions
Checks stock and orders or buys missing items in time, checking quality and dates
Writes a time plan working back from the serving time (long jobs first)
Sets up mise en place: ingredients prepared, equipment and plates ready
Works hygienically, cooks to the recipe, tastes, serves on time and cleans as they go

essays.stem: Explain how a cook uses temperature control to keep food safe, from delivery through to service.
essays.modelAnswer: Bacteria grow fastest in the danger zone, between about 5 °C and 63 °C, so a cook keeps food out of that range as much as possible (or as the Centre's food safety plan says). On delivery, chilled food is checked and put in the fridge at 5 °C or below straight away, and frozen food goes straight into the freezer. Frozen meat is thawed in the fridge, never on the counter. When cooking, poultry and minced meat are cooked to a core temperature of about 74 °C, checked with a clean probe thermometer in the thickest part. Hot food waiting for service is held at about 63 °C or above, for as short a time as possible. Leftovers are cooled quickly in shallow trays, then chilled, labelled and dated. Fridge and freezer temperatures are checked and written down every day, and any fault is reported at once.
markingPoints: Explains the danger zone (about 5 °C to 63 °C) where bacteria grow fast
Chilled food stored at 5 °C or below straight after delivery; frozen food thawed in the fridge
Poultry and minced meat cooked to about 74 °C, checked with a clean probe thermometer
Hot food held at about 63 °C or above; leftovers cooled quickly
Fridge and freezer temperatures checked, recorded, and faults reported

essays.stem: Explain what cross-contamination is and how to prevent it between raw and ready-to-eat foods in a small villa kitchen.
essays.modelAnswer: Cross-contamination is when bacteria pass from raw food, dirty hands or dirty equipment onto food that will not be cooked again, such as salad, fruit or cooked meat. To prevent it, I store raw meat and fish covered on the bottom shelf of the fridge, below cooked and ready-to-eat food, so their juices cannot drip onto it. I use separate chopping boards and knives for raw and ready-to-eat foods, using colour-coded boards if the Centre has them, or I wash and sanitise the board and knife between jobs. I wash my hands after touching raw meat and before touching anything else. Where I can, I prepare ready-to-eat food first or in a separate area. I clean and sanitise work tops, use clean cloths, and keep cooked food covered and away from raw food.
markingPoints: Explains cross-contamination: germs passing from raw food, hands or equipment to ready-to-eat food
Raw meat and fish stored covered, below ready-to-eat food
Separate (colour-coded) boards and knives, or washed and sanitised between jobs
Hands washed after touching raw food
Surfaces cleaned and sanitised; ready-to-eat food prepared first or apart, and kept covered

essays.stem: A guest tells you she has a shellfish allergy. Describe the steps you would take to prepare her meal safely.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would thank her, ask exactly what she cannot eat and how serious the allergy is, and tell my supervisor or head cook. I would check the recipe and the labels of every ingredient, including stocks, sauces and seasonings, for shrimp, crab, lobster or anything made from shellfish. I would choose a dish that has no shellfish in it at all. Before cooking, I would wash my hands and use clean boards, knives, pans and spoons that have not touched shellfish, and cook her meal on its own, never in oil or water already used for shrimp. I would cover her plate, label it with her name, and make sure the server knows which guest it is for. If I am not sure an item is safe, I do not serve it and I tell her honestly. If she shows signs of a reaction, I get help and call an ambulance at once.
markingPoints: Asks what she cannot eat and tells the supervisor and the server
Checks the recipe and every ingredient label, including stocks and sauces
Uses clean equipment and fresh oil or water, and cooks her meal apart
Labels her plate so it reaches the right guest
Is honest when not sure, and knows to get help at once if she reacts

essays.stem: Describe how to use, carry, clean and store kitchen knives safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I choose the right knife for the job, such as a paring knife for small work and a cook's knife for chopping, and I keep it sharp, because a blunt knife needs more force and is more likely to slip. I cut on a steady chopping board, with a damp cloth under it so it does not move, and I keep the fingers of my other hand curled back from the blade. I carry a knife point down, close to my side, and say "knife behind" when I pass people. I never leave a knife in a sink of soapy water where someone could put a hand on it, and I never try to catch a falling knife: I step back and let it fall. After use I wash the knife straight away, carefully, with the blade away from me, then dry it and store it in a knife block, rack or guard, not loose in a drawer.
markingPoints: Uses the right knife for the job and keeps it sharp
Cuts on a steady board with fingers curled back from the blade
Carries a knife point down and warns others
Never leaves a knife in the sink and never tries to catch a falling knife
Washes the knife straight after use and stores it in a block, rack or guard

essays.stem: Compare boiling, steaming and shallow frying as ways of cooking vegetables. For each, give one good point and one thing to take care with.
essays.modelAnswer: Boiling cooks vegetables in water at boiling point. It is quick and simple, and good for green bananas, yam and dumplings. The care point is not to overcook them, because vegetables go soft and lose colour and vitamins into the water, and a pot of boiling water can scald. Steaming cooks food in the steam above boiling water, with a lid on. It keeps more of the colour, shape and vitamins, so it suits callaloo, cabbage and carrots. Take care when lifting the lid, because steam burns: lift it away from you. Shallow frying cooks food in a little hot oil in a pan. It gives a tasty, golden outside, as with fried ripe plantain. The care points are that it adds fat, and hot oil can spit and burn, so the food should be dry and the pan never left alone.
markingPoints: Boiling: quick and simple (good point)
Boiling: avoid overcooking and loss of vitamins; boiling water can scald
Steaming: keeps colour, shape and vitamins
Steaming: steam burns, so lift the lid away from you
Shallow frying: tasty golden outside, but adds fat and hot oil spits; never leave the pan

essays.stem: Describe the steps to prepare and present ackee and saltfish for a villa breakfast, including how to make the ackee safe to eat.
essays.modelAnswer: I use only ripe ackee from pods that have opened naturally on the tree, or canned ackee from an approved source. I remove the black seeds and the pink-red membrane from each piece, wash the yellow flesh, and boil it gently in salted water until just tender, then throw that water away and drain the ackee. I soak the saltfish, then boil it once or twice in fresh water to take out most of the salt, cool it, and remove the skin and bones before flaking it. In a pan I sauté onion, escallion, sweet pepper, tomato, thyme and a little scotch bonnet pepper in a little oil, add the saltfish, then fold in the ackee gently so it does not break up. I taste it, then serve it hot on a warmed plate with fried dumpling, boiled green banana or roast breadfruit, add a small garnish, and wipe the rim clean before it goes out.
markingPoints: Uses only ackee from naturally opened pods (or approved canned ackee)
Removes the seeds and pink membrane, boils the ackee and throws the water away
Soaks and boils the saltfish to remove salt, then removes skin and bones and flakes it
Sautés the seasonings, adds the saltfish and folds in the ackee gently
Serves hot on a warmed plate with suitable sides, garnish and a clean rim

essays.stem: Explain what makes a plate of food look attractive to a guest. Describe at least four points.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the plate must be clean, with no chips or cracks, and the right size for the portion, so the food is not crowded or lost on it. Hot food goes on a warmed plate and cold food on a chilled one, so it reaches the guest at the right temperature. The food should have a mix of colours, such as green callaloo, orange carrot and golden fried plantain, and a mix of shapes and textures. Portions should be even and the right size, using the same spoon or ladle each time. The food is placed neatly, with the main item where the guest sees it first, and sauce is poured with care so it does not run everywhere. A small edible garnish, such as a sprig of thyme or a slice of lime, adds colour. Last, the rim is wiped clean with kitchen paper before the plate leaves the kitchen.
markingPoints: Clean plate with no chips, the right size for the portion
Right temperature: warmed plate for hot food, chilled plate for cold food
A mix of colours, shapes and textures
Even, neat portions placed with care; sauce controlled
A small edible garnish and a clean rim

essays.stem: Describe how to clean down the kitchen at the end of service, and say why each step matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I cover, label, date and put away any food that can be kept, so it stays safe and is not wasted, and I throw away anything that cannot be kept. I switch off and unplug equipment and let hot items cool, so no one is burnt or shocked. Then I scrape and wash pots, pans, boards and utensils in hot soapy water, rinse them, sanitise them and leave them to air-dry, because washing removes dirt and grease and sanitising kills germs. I wipe down the work tops, the stove and the inside of the fridge, cleaning first and then sanitising. I empty the bins, wash them and put in new liners, so pests are not attracted. Last, I sweep and mop the floor with a wet-floor sign out to prevent slips, put the cleaning chemicals away, and report any faults or low stock to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Covers, labels, dates and stores food that can be kept
Switches off and unplugs equipment safely
Washes, rinses and sanitises equipment, and explains why
Cleans and sanitises surfaces and empties and cleans the bins (pests)
Mops with a wet-floor sign, stores chemicals and reports faults or low stock

essays.stem: Explain how to cool, label, store and reheat leftover cooked rice and stew safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Cooked food must be cooled quickly so it does not stay long in the danger zone, where bacteria grow fast. Rice needs special care, because some bacteria found in rice can make poisons that reheating does not destroy. I would spread the rice and the stew into clean, shallow containers so they cool fast, and not leave them standing on the counter for hours. Once they have stopped steaming I would cover them and put them in the fridge at 5 °C or below, on a shelf above any raw meat. Each container gets a label saying what the food is and the date it was made. I would use the leftovers within the time the Centre's food safety plan allows, reheat them only once until they are piping hot all the way through, and throw away anything that is past its date or that I am not sure about.
markingPoints: Cools food quickly (danger zone), knowing rice needs special care
Uses shallow containers; does not leave food standing on the counter
Covers and chills at 5 °C or below, above raw meat
Labels with the name of the food and the date
Uses within the allowed time, reheats once until piping hot, and throws away doubtful food

practical1.title: Prepare and present a Jamaican breakfast for four guests
practical1.brief: Your group is the kitchen team at a villa. Prepare, cook and present a Jamaican breakfast for four guests (the assessor and other trainees play the guests): ackee and saltfish (canned ackee may be used), fried dumplings or festival, boiled green bananas, steamed callaloo, and a platter of sliced local fruit. First agree a written time plan and share out the dishes, so that every member prepares and cooks at least one item while the assessor watches, and every member helps with the plating and the clean-down. Serve the hot food hot and the fruit chilled, at the agreed time. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the kitchen is clean and the leftovers are stored.
materials: Saltfish, canned ackee (or fresh ackee from naturally opened pods), onion, escallion, tomato, sweet pepper, thyme and scotch bonnet pepper
Flour, cornmeal, baking powder, salt and sugar for dumplings or festival, and cooking oil
Green bananas, callaloo, and local fruit in season (pawpaw, pineapple, watermelon)
Pots, a frying pan, colour-coded boards, cook's and paring knives, a slotted spoon and tongs
Probe thermometer, plates, a platter and kitchen paper
Written recipes and a time-plan sheet
Washing-up liquid, sanitiser, cloths, gloves and a wet-floor sign
photos: The written time plan, showing each member's job
Mise en place: ingredients prepared and the work area set up
The saltfish boiled and flaked, and the ackee drained
Dumplings or festival frying, with the cook standing at the pan
The four breakfast plates and the fruit platter, plated and ready to serve
The kitchen cleaned down, and leftovers covered, labelled and dated
checklist: Arrived in clean uniform with hair covered, and washed hands before starting and between tasks
Took part in planning and kept to the time plan
Prepared ingredients safely, using the right board and knife, with no cross-contamination
Cooked at least one item correctly to the recipe and tasted it with a clean spoon
Handled hot oil and boiling water safely and never left a pan alone
Plated food neatly on clean plates, with clean rims and at the right temperature
Took part in the clean-down: washed and sanitised equipment, and stored and labelled food
safety: Never leave hot oil alone; dry food before frying, and keep a lid and fire blanket close by
Carry knives point down, and never try to catch a falling knife
Wipe spills at once and put out a wet-floor sign
Keep raw and ready-to-eat food apart, and keep cold food at 5 °C or below (or as the Centre's food safety plan says)
Read cleaning product labels, wear gloves and never mix chemicals; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Prepare and present a two-course lunch: pumpkin soup, then brown stew chicken with rice and peas and salad
practical2.brief: Your group prepares a two-course lunch for four villa guests: a starter of pumpkin soup, then brown stew chicken with rice and peas and a fresh garden salad. First write a short order list and a time plan. Share the dishes so that every member is in charge of one dish (soup, chicken, rice and peas, or salad) and helps with a second dish while the assessor watches; a fifth member, if there is one, is in charge of plating and the final checks, and helps with the soup. Check the chicken's core temperature with a probe thermometer and write it down. Serve each course on warmed (or, for the salad, chilled) plates at the agreed time. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the kitchen is clean and the leftovers are stored.
materials: Pumpkin, onion, garlic, escallion, thyme, stock and seasoning for the soup
Chicken pieces, browning, onion, sweet pepper, tomato, thyme, pimento and cooking oil
Rice, canned red kidney beans, coconut milk, escallion and thyme
Lettuce, tomato, cucumber, carrot and a simple dressing
Pots, a heavy pan, colour-coded boards, knives, a ladle, a blender or masher, and a probe thermometer
Soup bowls, dinner plates, a salad bowl and kitchen paper
Order list and time-plan sheet, labels and a marker
Washing-up liquid, sanitiser, cloths, gloves and a wet-floor sign
photos: The order list and time plan, with each member's dish
Raw chicken being prepared on its own board, away from the salad
The probe thermometer in the chicken, showing the core temperature
The soup served in bowls for the first course
The main course plated with chicken, rice and peas and salad
Leftovers cooled, covered, labelled and dated in the fridge, and the kitchen clean
checklist: Worked hygienically: clean uniform, hair covered, hands washed at the right times
Helped to write the order list and time plan, and kept to it
Kept raw chicken apart from the salad and other ready-to-eat food
Cooked their dish correctly to the recipe, tasting with a clean spoon
Checked that the chicken reached about 74 °C in the thickest part (or as the Centre's food safety plan says)
Served each course at the right time and temperature, with even portions and clean rims
Cooled, labelled and stored leftovers correctly and took part in the clean-down
safety: Blend hot soup in small amounts with the lid on and held down; never put a hand in the blender jug
Use oven cloths for hot pots, and turn pan handles inward, away from the edge of the stove
Wash hands after handling raw chicken, and wash and sanitise its board and knife
Wipe spills at once and put out a wet-floor sign
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for all equipment and cleaning chemicals
